extracted.intended_audience: Isabelle/Pure users and implementers (proof-engine developers, tool authors, advanced Isabelle/jEdit users)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal rules for specifying, printing, parsing, and transforming Isabelle/Pure inner syntax (mixfix notation, priority grammars, tokens, AST translations, and print modes). Targeted at people defining notations, syntax translations, or writing tools that operate on Isabelle terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic printing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: typ, term, prop, thm, prf, full_prf, print_state: diagnostic commands that print internal logical entities in a human-readable fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typ/term/prop to read, type-check and print types, terms or propositions according to the current theory/proof context; inferred type is output. Use thm a1 ... an to retrieve theorems (attributes in specs are applied to a temporary context and do not have permanent effect). Use prf to display the compact proof term (requires a logic image with proof terms enabled); full_prf displays the full proof term (expands '_' placeholders). Use print_state to print the current proof state including goals and current facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: typ τ :: s behaviour and dummy type parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: typ τ :: s uses type-inference to determine the most general way to make τ conform to sort s. Dummy type parameters '_' are assigned fresh type variables with most general sorts per type-inference principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For concrete τ this checks membership in sort s. Rely on Isabelle's inference for underspecified types; use explicit constraints if you need more precise control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print detail options (show_markup)
rubrics_metrics.description: show_markup controls direct inlining of markup into the printed representation of formal entities — notably type and sort constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable show_markup to allow IDEs (Isabelle/jEdit) to show type/sort information via tooltips/popups. show_consts_markup requires show_markup and controls printing of type constraints for term constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print detail options (show_types / show_sorts)
rubrics_metrics.description: show_types and show_sorts control printing of type constraints for term variables, and sort constraints for type variables; by default neither are shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable when you need explicit types/sorts in output (helps explain polymorphic inference failures or why rewrite rules don't apply). Note: show_markup often makes these unnecessary in Isabelle/jEdit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print detail options (show_consts / show_abbrevs)
rubrics_metrics.description: show_consts controls printing of types of constants when displaying a goal state; show_abbrevs controls folding of constant abbreviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that show_consts output can be enormous (polymorphic constants at many instances). Use show_abbrevs to fold abbreviations for brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name printing modes (names_long / names_short / names_unique)
rubrics_metrics.description: names_long, names_short and names_unique control how fully qualified internal names are printed in external form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick one to control verbosity of names in output; consult §4.2 for document antiquotation options with the same names. Use names_unique to avoid ambiguous unqualified names.

rubrics_metrics.name: eta_contract printing option
rubrics_metrics.description: eta_contract controls η-contracted printing of terms (apply η-contraction before printing so that λh. F (λx. h x) prints as F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you prefer η-contracted, more compact printed terms. Note that the distinction sometimes matters: some tools look at terms discretely even though many operations are modulo αβη-conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: goals_limit and show_main_goal
rubrics_metrics.description: goals_limit controls the maximum number of subgoals to be printed; show_main_goal controls whether the main result to be proven is displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust goals_limit to avoid overwhelming output. show_main_goal is useful for inspecting schematic goals synthesized so far.

rubrics_metrics.name: show_hyps, show_tags, show_question_marks
rubrics_metrics.description: show_hyps controls printing of implicit hypotheses of local facts; show_tags controls printing of extra annotations (e.g., internal position info, case names); show_question_marks controls printing of leading '?' for schematic variables like ?x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable show_hyps to force printing of all hypotheses for diagnostics. Use show_tags to reveal low-level annotations. show_question_marks affects only the leading '?' character and can aid readability in UIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print-mode facility
rubrics_metrics.description: print_mode_value returns the list of currently active print mode names; Print_Mode.with_modes prepends given modes to the current print mode for executing a function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print modes to symbolically enable/disable alternative pretty-printer productions. Modes are thread-safe and monotonic (they prepend to the current mode list). Common conventional mode names include "" (default), input (dummy), internal (dummy), ASCII, and latex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mixfix annotations for concrete syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixfix annotations specify concrete inner syntax of Isabelle types and terms, describing concrete syntax, translation to abstract syntax, and pretty printing. They may be given during declaration or via notation commands later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer mixfix annotations to cover most concrete-syntax needs without understanding deeper syntax engine layers. Special-case annotations provide simple infix and binder specs. Mixfix is powerful enough to express any context-free priority grammar.

rubrics_metrics.name: General mixfix form and priority conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A mixfix annotation is a template d0 _ d1 _ ... _ dn together with priority list [p1,...,pn] and result priority p; priorities are optional with defaults (0 for arguments, 1000 for result). Nested/partial applications: notation is attached to innermost part; if fewer arguments than template then concrete syntax is ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting priorities can cause ambiguities unless delimiters fully bracket notation. Use explicit priorities to control binding power; remember defaults: arg default 0, result default 1000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixfix template entities (delimiters, underscores, index, blocks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates may include delimiters (sequence of items), '_' for argument positions, 'ı' for indexed argument (implicit structure reference), space sequences, pretty-printing blocks '(n' or '(‹properties›', and break /s or // for line breaking control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-quote ' to escape meta-characters; use cartouches for properties. Blocks control indentation and allow sophisticated line-breaking/formatting behavior for pretty printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixfix block properties and notation kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported block properties: indent, open_block, consistent, unbreakable, markup, notation (cartouche). notation kinds include mixfix, prefix, postfix, infix, binder, literal, type_application, application, abstraction, judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set 'consistent' to force all breaks in a block to be taken together; 'unbreakable' disables breaks. Use 'markup' to attach PIDE XML attributes for IDE integration. Use notation kind to declare the nature of the block for documentation and tooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infix shortcut annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: infix, infixl, infixr provide short forms for common infix mixfix declarations, mapping to templates like "(_ sy/ _)" with adjusted priorities: infix adds [p+1,p+1] p, infixl [p,p+1] p, infixr [p+1,p] p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these shortcuts for most infix operator declarations; the template includes a pretty-printing block with space/line-break rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binder annotations for variable-binding constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Binder annotation syntax c :: "(τ1 ⇒ τ2) ⇒ τ3" (binder "sy" [p] q) introduces concrete binder syntax sy x. b with x bound of type τ1 and body of type τ2; optional p is body priority (default q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binder annotations are expanded internally to dedicated mixfix templates (e.g., c_binder :: "idts ⇒ τ2 ⇒ τ3" ("(3sy_./ _)" [0,p] q)). The syntax translation transforms binder-form into iterated λ-applications for parsing and printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit notation commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands: type_notation, no_type_notation, notation, no_notation, write — to add or remove mixfix annotations for types/constants/fixed variables. write works inside Isar proof bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to modify notation for existing logical entities within the current context. no_* variants remove specified annotations. The arity/type info is retrieved from the context automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inner lexical token categories and delimiter precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Inner lexical categories are fixed (id, longid, var, tid, tvar, num_token, float_token, str_token, string_token, cartouche). Delimiters override named tokens and may make certain identifiers inaccessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful when introducing delimiters that could shadow identifiers. Object-logics can add literals by appropriate syntax declarations and translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority grammar conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority grammars decorate nonterminals with integer priorities between 0 and 1000 and use derivation rules A(p) -> A(q)=γ only if p ≤ q. Conventions: all priorities between 0 and 1000; omit 0 on RHS and 1000 on LHS; write production A = α (p); alternatives separated by |; repetition indicated informally by '...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use priorities to control operator binding and associativity. Translate priority grammars to regular CFGs conceptually when needed. Follow notation conventions to keep grammars readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of core Pure grammar categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pure grammar distinguishes categories: any (any term), prop (meta-level propositions), aprop (atomic propositions embedded by PROP), logic (terms of logical types excluding prop), index, idt, idts, pttrn, pttrns, type, sort, class_name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When specifying notation, collapse all logical types (excluding prop) to 'logic'. Use aprop/PROP where terms of type prop with non-constant head need to be embedded. Refer to the grammar for correct priorities of constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Underscore (_) roles and dummy variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The underscore '_' has multiple roles: as a sort '_', it is a vacuous constraint; as a type '_', it is an anonymous inference parameter; as a bound '_' it is a vacuous abstraction; as a free '_' it is an implicit outer binding; as a schematic '_' in patterns it is an anonymous variable implicitly abstracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of context when using '_': its meaning depends on where it appears. Use explicit parentheses to disambiguate interpretations in sequences of idts or type-constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONST and XCONST semantics in syntax translations
rubrics_metrics.description: CONST ensures the given identifier is treated as a constant term and passed through the parse tree fully internalized. XCONST is similar but retains the constant name as given; both are relevant to translation rules, notably CONST on RHS and XCONST on LHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONST/XCONST in translation patterns when you need to force constant treatment and avoid accidental variable capture or re-interpretation during translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspecting the current syntax with print_syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: print_syntax prints the inner syntax of the current context. Important sections include lexicon (delimiters), productions (priority grammar), print modes, parse_rules/print_rules (syntax translations/macros), parse_ast_translation/print_ast_translation, and parse_translation/print_translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use print_syntax to debug grammar/notational issues; expect large output. Look for productions that have '. . . => name' (these are parse-tree heads) and identify copy/chain productions which have special behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling parsing ambiguity and filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Isabelle's Earley parser can enumerate multiple parse trees; terms that cannot be type-checked are filtered out. Parsing fails if multiple results remain after filtering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use syntax_ambiguity_warning to control printing of explicit ambiguity warnings and syntax_ambiguity_limit to set how many parse trees are shown. Remember that filtering does not consider whole-term collection context (unlike some type reconstruction), so ambiguous inputs can persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax transformation pipeline and when to use it
rubrics_metrics.description: Parsing/printing pipeline involves lexer+parser, parse tree → AST, AST rewriting (macros), parse translation, pre-term, check/uncheck and type-inference, and corresponding print translations. Transformations happen via AST rewrite systems (§8.5.2) or ML functions (§8.5.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a rule of thumb: anything that manipulates bindings or scopes must be implemented as a syntax transformation; tasks that don't manipulate bindings are better done via check/uncheck layers (e.g., abbreviations). Carefully pass-through type and binding information when writing transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AST datatype and distinction between Constant and Variable
rubrics_metrics.description: The intermediate AST format is datatype ast = Constant of string | Variable of string | Appl of ast list. Constants are shown as quoted strings, variables as unquoted, applications as parenthesized lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AST is first-order: AST constants do not bind variables. Use Ast.Constant for known constants to prevent accidental reinterpretation later; leave Ast.Variable where scope/resolution should be resolved by later layers. Avoid creating ASTs with too few subtrees (() or (x) are invalid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic syntax names for robust AST transformations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentic syntax names are fully-qualified constant names with a special prefix for their formal category (class, type, const, fixed) to represent information faithfully inside untyped ASTs and avoid accidental overlap with free/bound variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic syntax names in transformations to avoid surprises due to later name resolution. They arise implicitly in input of notation-introduced term constants, type constants/classes, and output of fully-known internal terms.
